explanation: Queen Maria I and the prince regent, João, sailed under British escort, and the court ruled the empire from Rio until 1821. Brazil declared independence a year later.
learnMore: Transfer of the Portuguese court to Brazil

claims.text: The Portuguese royal court moved to Rio de Janeiro in 1808, fleeing Napoleon's invasion of Portugal.
The royal courts of Spain, Denmark and the Netherlands did not move to Rio de Janeiro.
Queen Maria I and the prince regent João sailed to Brazil under British naval escort.
The Portuguese court ruled from Rio de Janeiro until 1821.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Flight from Napoleon: French and Spanish forces invaded Portugal in late 1807, and John ordered the Portuguese court to be transferred to Brazil before he could be deposed. The fleet sailed in late November 1807, just days before Napoleonic forces invaded Portugal on 1 December 1807. Arrival: The court did not go straight to Rio. On 22 January 1808, Prince John and his court arrived in Salvador, Brazil. In March 1808, the court arrived in Rio de Janeiro.

claimResults.note: The fleet left Lisbon in late November 1807 as Napoleon's forces invaded; the court reached Salvador in January 1808 and Rio de Janeiro in March 1808.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Return to Lisbon: The Liberal Revolution of 1820 forced the issue. Sources differ on the departure date: one gives 25 April 1821, while another says the return of John VI of Portugal on 26 April 1821. Arrival in Lisbon is given as 4 July 1821, while another source says the ships arrived in Lisbon on 3 July.

claimResults.note: Joao VI sailed from Rio for Lisbon in April 1821 (25 or 26 April, by source) and arrived in July 1821; the day varies between sources, the year does not.
